newsitem.title: USA: U.S. troops to head for Kuwait next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. troops to head for Kuwait next week.

text.p: The first units of a total of 1,200 U.S. troops will begin flying from Fort Hood, Texas, to Kuwait next week for the latest in a series of joint military exercises since the 1991 Gulf War.

The troops from the First Cavalry Division at Fort Hood will join heavy U.S. armour already stationed in the Gulf emirate and will remain there for about four months as part of "Exercise Intrinsic Action 97-1," the Pentagon said.
The United States and Kuwait signed a defence cooperation agreement after a U.S.-led military coalition drove occupying Iraqi troops from Kuwait.

The U.S. Embassy in Kuwait this week said the American troops would draw on heavy armour including main battle tanks that Washington has pre-positioned at Kuwait's Camp Doha for quick use in case of a new Gulf crisis.
In a fresh standoff with Baghdad, Washington last September ordered some 3,000 ground troops to Kuwait in addition to about 1,200 that were taking part in an earlier Intrinsic Action exercise.
The ground troops left late last year but eight radar-avoiding Stealth bombers that were sent to Kuwait at the time of the crisis remain in the small Gulf Arab state.
